cases.answer:
Federal law, specifically $\S 435.2$ of the FTC Mail, Internet, or telephone order sales rule, requires that if a seller cannot ship merchandise within the time stated in the solicitation, they must offer the buyer, clearly and conspicuously and without prior demand, an option to either consent to a delay or to cancel the order and receive a prompt refund. This offer must be made within a reasonable time after the seller first becomes aware of the inability to ship, but no later than the applicable time.

The rule also specifies:
*   If a definite revised shipping date is provided that is 30 days or less later than the original time, the buyer is deemed to have consented unless they reject the delay and cancel the order before the revised date.
*   If the revised date is more than 30 days later, or if no definite revised date can be provided, the buyer is informed that the order will automatically be deemed cancelled unless they expressly consent to the delay within 30 days of the original time.
*   The buyer retains a continuing right to cancel the order at any time before actual shipment, even if they consented to an indefinite delay.

(Source: ftc_mail_order_rule_16cfr435.xml)
